title: Influence of magnetic fields on the performance of spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory
authors: Jiaxin Liu, Yuqing Zhou, Guoyi Shi, Kaiming Cai
abstract: Spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory (SOT-MRAM) offers high speed, ultrahigh endurance, and compatibility with advanced semiconductor processes, making it a promising candidate for next-generation nonvolatile memory. However, intrinsic bias fields in magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), originating from reference-layer stray fields and interlayer coupling, cause asymmetric critical switching currents and increased energy consumption. Existing compensation approaches usually introduce additional magnetic layers into the MTJ stack, which increases fabrication complexity and limits wafer-scale integration. Here, we propose a bias-compensation strategy without modifying the MTJ stack by engineering local stray magnetic fields through magnetic filling materials in vertical interconnect access (VIA) channels during the back-end-of-line process. Micromagnetic simulations show that the proposed magnetic filling layer can provide the required auxiliary field for deterministic switching and significantly suppress write-current asymmetry. By optimizing the MTJ position relative to the magnetic filling structure, the write-current bias ratio is reduced from 21.6% in the conventional design to 1.3%. The approach is also applicable to in-plane magnetic anisotropy SOT-MTJs, reducing the bias ratio from 19.8% to -0.2%. Scaling analysis further demonstrates that the compensation effect remains effective when the device size is reduced to 20% of the original dimension (MTJ diameter approximately 10 nm), indicating its potential for high-density SOT-MRAM integration.
summary: This paper addresses performance limitations in SOT-MRAM caused by intrinsic stray magnetic bias fields. The authors propose a novel, non-invasive method using magnetic filling in interconnect vias to compensate for this bias field. This technique significantly reduces switching current asymmetry, making the memory more energy-efficient and scalable for future integration.
main_problem: SOT-MRAM suffers from an intrinsic bias field due to stray fields, causing asymmetric critical switching currents and increased energy consumption.
main_result: The authors propose engineering local stray magnetic fields via magnetic filling in VIA channels, reducing the write-current bias ratio from 21.6% to 1.3% and maintaining performance at nanoscale dimensions.
method: The study uses micromagnetic simulations to model the effect of engineered local stray fields on the magnetization switching dynamics of SOT-MRAM.
model_or_system: The physical system is Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Random-Access Memory (SOT-MRAM) devices, analyzed using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation incorporating SOT terms for both PMA and IMA structures.
key_observables: Write-current asymmetry, write-current bias ratio, power consumption, and data-retention stability.
important_parameters: Bias magnetic field (H_s), critical current densities (J_AP->P, J_P->AP), and device size (down to 10 nm diameter).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that modifying VIA channels with ferromagnetic material can effectively modulate the stray field without altering the sensitive MTJ thin films.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the asymmetry in switching fields and currents due to bias fields, and show the modulation of the bias ratio and current density using the proposed magnetic filling structure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of bias-induced asymmetry in SOT-MRAM, then proposes the non-invasive BEOL-compatible field engineering technique, and finally quantifies the resulting improvements in switching symmetry and power consumption.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the concept of engineering local fields to control switching dynamics is relevant to understanding engineered quantum potentials or controlling interactions in artificial quantum systems.

Figure 4 presents the simulation results for the PMA structure. To achieve deterministic switching of the free layer driven by current in the PMA structure, an auxiliary field Hx along the x-direction is typically required. As shown in Figure 4(a), when the external magnetic field is small, the critical switching current density Jc decreases linearly with increasing Hx, and the direction of Hx determines the switching polarity. Furthermore, when a magnetic field Hy along the y-direction is introduced under a fixed auxiliary field of μ0Hx = 60 mT, the modulation of Jc by Hy exhibits nonlinear characteristics, as illustrated in Figure 4(b).
